definition: To do what a rule, request, or order says you must do.
example: Every restaurant in town must comply with the new food safety rules by spring.
nuance: Comply usually takes "with" and suggests meeting a rule or request, while obey stresses yielding to a person's authority.
prompt: A school library posts a new rule asking students to silence their phones.
options: Most students were glad to comply and set their phones to silent.
The librarian complied the new rule from three older policies.
To comply with the rule, Ava turned her ringer up to full volume.
Jamal complied about the rule to anyone in the library who would listen.
reasons: Silencing their phones is exactly what the posted rule asked students to do.
Putting together material from several sources is compiling, not following a rule.
Making the phone louder goes against the rule instead of following it.
Grumbling about a rule is complaining; the word means going along with it.

practice.prompt: A soccer referee tells a player to tuck in his jersey before the match.
options: The midfielder complied by pulling his jersey out even further than before.
The referee complied the player to fix his uniform right away.
His striped jersey complied nicely with his bright red socks and cleats.
The midfielder was quick to comply and tucked his shirt in before kickoff.
reasons: Doing the opposite of an instruction is defiance, not obedience.
The person who follows the order complies; the word cannot mean forcing someone.
Clothes that look good together complement each other; they do not follow rules.
He did what the referee asked, which is what following an instruction means.
